artboards.title: After — charges are rows of the document

annotations.text:
CHARGES BELONG TO THE QUOTE, NOT BESIDE IT

Every value here is read out of index.html — the eight-track grid at :6109, the ghost input at :12749, the foot at :6185, the shop-side divider at :6117 — and the palette is the house 23. Nothing is drawn to taste.

The move: a charge stops being a panel under the table and becomes a ROW OF THE TABLE. It rides the same eight tracks, so its figure lands in the line-total column, under the figures it is added to. That is the law the foot already keeps and the block below it could not.

WHAT IS WRONG, MEASURED

1. 5,000 UGX sits ~280px right of the 155,000 UGX it is added to. Money that does not line up is unreadable at a glance — and a glance is the only way money is read.

2. The input is the heaviest object on screen: a permanently boxed control with a native stepper, so a 5,000 fee out-weighs a 155,000 line.

3. A rule, a heading, a sentence, ~900px of empty row, a detached chip strip — and the shop-side divider stops dead above it.

WHAT MARKS IT AS NOT A GOOD IS WHAT IT HAS NOT GOT

No number in the gutter, no quantity, no supplier, no margin. Three empty cells and a name at 500 rather than 600 — no tint band, no badge, no second state colour, because a device that marks everything marks nothing.

The typed figure goes in PRICE EACH and what it comes to in LINE TOTAL, exactly as a quantity-of-one item already does. The add row is the "Add the next item" row's twin, carrying the shop's own services with their usual amounts.

The two subtotals leave the foot: with each charge a visible row directly above it, "Items / Charges" restated what was already on screen. Second row shown hovered — the × and the input's border appear on hover, as on every other row.

THE CASE THE FIXED ROW DOES NOT SHOW

A percent charge has two genuinely different figures, and they land in the two columns that already mean those things: you type 5 in PRICE EACH, it comes to 67,500 in LINE TOTAL. The sub-line says what the percent is OF, because a percent with no basis is not a figure.

Every percent resolves against the goods, never a running total — so two of them never compound, whichever was tapped first.

820 IS A SWITCH, NOT A REFLOW

A charge is a card like an item card, minus the two facts it has not got — the same marker as the console, in the phone's own grammar. 15px body, 44px remove target, chips at 38px.

The old block put the name, the input, the amount and the × on one 390px line; the × wrapped to a line of its own and read as belonging to nothing.
